title: How Planes Are Cleared for Takeoff
introduction: Learn how an aircraft moves from being ready for departure to receiving clearance to take off.

interactiveConcepts.title: Takeoff Sequence
interactiveConcepts.description: Follow an aircraft from its parking position through taxiing and takeoff clearance.

interactiveConcepts.title: ATC Communication
interactiveConcepts.description: Explore the communication between pilots and air traffic control.

interactiveConcepts.title: Clearance Sequence
interactiveConcepts.description: Step through holding short, line up and wait, and cleared for takeoff.

glossary.definition: Air Traffic Control, which manages and coordinates aircraft movements.
A designated route used by aircraft to move between airport areas and runways.
An ATC authorization allowing an aircraft to begin its takeoff.
An instruction for an aircraft to enter the runway, align for departure and wait for further clearance.

testYourself.question: Who normally gives the final takeoff clearance?
testYourself.explanation: Air Traffic Control gives the aircraft its takeoff clearance when the runway and surrounding traffic situation allow it to depart safely.

testYourself.question: What does a pilot normally do if a takeoff instruction is unclear?
testYourself.explanation: The pilot should clarify an unclear instruction with ATC rather than guessing or proceeding without understanding it.

testYourself.question: What is a taxiway used for?
testYourself.explanation: Taxiways provide the routes aircraft use to move between parking areas, runways and other parts of the airport.
